abstract: Let $S$, $S'$ be K3 surfaces with trivial endomorphism field and $\operatorname{rk}T$ odd or at least $10$. The Hodge conjecture for their products reduces to two statements: the determinant class is algebraic, and Hodge similarities $T(S)\to T(S')$ of nonsquare multiplier are algebraic ($\Psi_{\mathrm{ns}}$). No nonsquare case is known at Picard rank one. Two mechanisms move algebraic classes across moduli: twistor transport of hyperholomorphic sheaves (Buskin, Markman) and deformation of Lagrangian submanifolds (Voisin). For each, we determine what a seed must satisfy and where it stops. (1) A rational class that stays Hodge along a path through a point with Picard group $0$ and induces a multiple of a Hodge similarity on $T$ is a similarity of all of $H^2$. Hence twistor transport between hyperkähler manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$- and $K3^{[m]}$-type reaches only multipliers congruent to $(n-1)(m-1)$ modulo squares. (2) Irreducible Lagrangian correspondences of degrees $a,b$ satisfy $ab\equiv\lambda$ for K3 surfaces, and have multiplier $\sqrt{a^3b}$ for $K3^{[2]}$-type. Lagrangian-type cycles on $S^m$ with $m=\operatorname{rk}T$ odd have no determinant component. (3) The graph closure of the fibrewise complex multiplication $[1-\omega]$ on $y^2=x^3+f_{12}(t)$ is a singular Lagrangian. Its class stays Hodge and Lagrangian on a $19$-dimensional family, but at a very general point no effective cycle has this class. (4) For cubic fourfolds, Hecke partners of multiplier $\lambda$ exist iff $\lambda$ is a norm from $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. On Eisenstein cubics, line constructions by incidences and spans stay in a tangent hyperplane section, and those we analyzed give only square norms. One natural norm-$3$ map, from the Fano variety to the Lehn–Lehn–Sorger–van Straten eightfold, has the type the parity rule allows. But, granted a transversality hypothesis checked only numerically, its graph is not trianalytic: it pulls the polarization back to at least $3g$, while $g$ is required. No new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Limited revision of v1, following the decision on the previous revision request. Proposition 2.4 and Proposition 5.2(c) of that request are NOT included; they will be developed in a separate submission. Changes: (1) Abstract: the opening reduction now states the rank hypothesis (rk T odd or at least 10). (2) Section 1.1 defines the determinant class D and says why it is a Hodge class. (3) Proposition 3.2 now states that Y is projective. Its proof shows directly that the transcendental part T(Y)_Q is irreducible: q is nondegenerate on it and it has no nonzero rational (1,1)-class, so a sub-Hodge structure either is of type (1,1), hence zero, or contains sigma, and then its orthogonal complement is of type (1,1), hence zero. This replaces a sentence of the previous request that claimed irreducibility for every polarizable Hodge structure of K3 type with h^{2,0} = 1, which is false. It also notes that f^*, g^* are injective on H^2, which gives f^*T(Y) = g^*T(Y'). (4) Proposition 4.1(d), case b = 3: explains why ramification of the base map does not affect the Euler-number count (an I_1 fibre over a point of ramification index r pulls back to I_r). (5) Section 1.2: Proposition 5.3 is marked as conditional on (T), and a status line separates the conditional parts (b)-(c) from the unconditional results. (6) Appendix A, prodsum.py item: the twisted Chern character convention on Z is stated, and both q(theta) = 2 and div(theta) = 2 are used for the splitting H^2(Z,Z) = Z theta + T(Z). (7) Section 1.1: a short paragraph on a third mechanism, deformation of semiregular sheaves (new references [24]-[26]), noting that Lemma 2.1 constrains it only along paths through a point with Picard group 0. (8) Section 6, Lagrangian bullet: as in [9, Thm 4(a), Section 6.3], a graph seed between K3 surfaces with multiplier other than 1 that deforms to Picard rank one yields a dominant rational map of degree at least 2 onto a K3 surface of Picard rank one. Karzhemanov-Konovalov (new reference [27]) state that no such map exists. With an explicit cross-reference to [9, Remark 5.2], the consequence is stated only conditionally. No other results changed; the supplement is that of v1.
title: Transporting nonsquare Hodge similarities of K3 type: two mechanisms and where they stop
